newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle trade Tuesday was slow, with light sales steady with last week's top of $72.00 per cwt on a live basis, feedlot sources said.

About 400 head, mostly steers, traded at $72.00 in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said. An estimated 800 head were also sold at $72.00 in Kansas, according to USDA and private sources.
The bulk of this week's showlist was being offered for sale at $74.00 or more, with packers generally bidding $72.00, sources said.
Prices were supported by sharply higher boxed beef prices the past two days, sources said.

Choice heavyweight beef values climbed $4.89 per cwt since Friday, with the midday value Tuesday quoted by USDA up $1.77 at $109.72. The midday quote put the choice heavyweight value at the highest level since November 3, 1995.
Beef price gains were powered by tight stocks following two weeks of light slaughter and strong demand, sources said.
